why: B's hand-written IsScFredholmB has exactly the fields of the project's ScFredholmSplitting (repackaged by isScFredholmB_iff), and T.add S.toScOperator is definitionally T + S.toScOperator, so proposition_1_1_11_preprint is literally B (A_to_B). B still gives proposition_1_1_11_preprint and the bootstrap lemma ScPlus.regularizing_add (B plus Proposition 1.9; kept as B_to_A_old). But A now also contains the criterion isScFredholm_of_isRegularizing(_index): an sc-operator that is Fredholm on level 0 and regularizing is sc-Fredholm, with the level-0 index on every level. B (sc-Fredholm + sc⁺ is sc-Fredholm) says nothing about operators not already sc-Fredholm; the criterion needs the construction of §1.4.1 (Prop. 1.6 for the kernel, density of smooth points in the range, a smooth complement), i.e. re-proving the project's argument, and every project route to it goes through the banned lemma. So B ⇒ A fails for content B does not state.
overlap: B_to_A_old (B ⇒ proposition_1_1_11_preprint ∧ regularizing_add): 36 shared project theorems, structure-field projections and glue (ScFredholmSplitting fields, toBase/levelSub/shift lemmas, ScOperator.add proofs) plus proposition_1_1_10, K_le_smooth and proposition_1_1_7_iff; nothing of the perturbation argument is reused. No full B_to_A.
